Maya: Quick thread — I'd like feedback on a compact p99 attribution widget for per-route KPIs. Goal: show p50/p95/p99 plus a stacked attribution bar that breaks down token-level latency into kernel selection, batching wait, KV cache hit/miss, and token generation. Mockup below.

Maya: Proposed UX: single small card per route with: 1) p50/p95/p99 numbers, 2) rps, 3) error rate, 4) stacked bar where each segment is percent of p99 latency (kernel/batch/kv/queue/other). Clicking opens full drilldown.

Phil: SGTM. How do you plan to attribute latency to kernel vs batching? We currently only emit total token_latency and kernel_latency in micro-bench traces.

Sanjay: We can approximate by: token_latency = kernel_exec + batching_wait + kv_lookup + serialization. We already emit kernel_exec and kv_lookup. Need to add batching_wait and queue_time labels from runtime.

Eva: +1. We should avoid per-request labels explosion. Suggest aggregate histograms with tag 'route' and 'kernel_variant' and a separate 'step' metric that logs step durations as events.

Maya: Agreed on tagging. Idea: emit per-token spans as short events in tracing (step=kernel|batch_wait|kv), then a nightly job compiles attribution percentages for p90/p95/p99 per route.

Phil: How easy is it to compute p99 attribution from histograms? We'll need percentile decomposition. Suggest we store bucketed counts for each step and approximate with weighted sampling.

Sanjay: We prototyped this in local perf runs. Sample script:
```
SELECT route, percentile_approx(total_latency,0.99) AS p99_total,
  percentile_approx(kernel,0.99) AS p99_kernel,
  percentile_approx(batch_wait,0.99) AS p99_batch,
  percentile_approx(kv,0.99) AS p99_kv
FROM token_spans
WHERE ts > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY route;
```
Results looked reasonable but sometimes p99_total > sum(parts) due to skew — need to compute attribution via sampling of same requests.

Eva: For correctness, we must attribute on the same request. So computing percentiles per-field independently is wrong. Either do request-level sampling or compute contributions as averages conditioned on tail requests.

Zoe: UX note: display 'attribution confidence' when attribution was computed via sampling and show sample size.

Phil: Ops question: will this increase telemetry volume? Emitting per-token spans sounds heavy.

Maya: We'll start with a conservative plan: enable per-token step spans for 1% of requests per route for 24h when a route is onboarded. For routes with significant tail issues we can bump to 10%.

Sanjay: Also we can emit aggregated step histograms from the runtime every minute to avoid per-token events. That cuts volume by ~100x.

ops-bot: perf-profiling-job #834 completed: sample=1% routes={chat,search}, duration=24h, artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/834

Phil: Nice. Can someone upload a quick mockup of the mini-card for Console? Prefer a horizontal layout: left stats, right stacked bar + small sparkline.

Maya: Uploaded quick mock here: https://figma.redwood.com/file/abcd/kpi-mini-card (mock shows 3-label stacked bar with hover breakdown, click-to-open drilldown)

Eva: Also include a small dropdown to switch attribution basis: 'per-request sample' vs 'histogram approximation'.

Sanjay: I'll add the telemetry changes as a PR to runtime tomorrow: add batch_wait and per-route sampling flag. ETA EOD.

Phil: Thanks. Next: define alerts. I'd like an alert rule: if p99 attribution to kernel increases by >20% week-over-week AND absolute p99_total > 200ms => page.

Maya: Good rule. Also add a 'cost alert' if batching_wait increases while kernel cost drops (possible mismatch in batch sizing).

Zoe: UX follow-up: card needs to show sample size and last-updated timestamp.

Maya: Great. Action items: 1) Sanjay PR for telemetry, 2) Ops-profiling schedule update (I'll coordinate), 3) Phil to draft alert rules, 4) Eva to add UX dropdown. We'll reconvene after PR lands.

Phil: Thanks all :thumbsup:
